portfolio.title: Investment Club Portfolio
portfolio.subtitle: Stock Picks, Holdings Review & Recommendations
portfolio.week_narrative: In plain terms: stocks had a good week because the U.S. and Iran moved toward ending their war, which pushed oil prices down and made investors feel safer — that matters to you because cheaper oil means cheaper gas and less inflation pressure on your wallet, and a calmer world usually means your investments grow. With a U.S.-Iran resolution now in sight, Wall Street turned more optimistic at the year's halfway mark: JPMorgan hiked its 2026 S&P 500 target to 7,800 from 7,200, suggesting another 5% rise from current levels is possible. The catch — Thursday's PCE report showed inflation at its highest in roughly three years, but it also confirmed that consumer spending remains robust, suggesting the U.S. economy can absorb what many hope is a one-time spike in energy prices. The Federal Reserve (the U.S. central bank that sets interest rates) kept the fed funds rate unchanged at the 3.5%–3.75% target range for a third consecutive meeting, signaling patience. Beneath the surface, money rotated OUT of the biggest AI names (Alphabet, Meta, Nvidia softened) and INTO smaller companies and value plays — the Russell 2000 has surged nearly 21%, while the S&P 500 has added less than 10% in 2026. China also slapped MP Materials and USA Rare Earth with export controls, a reminder that supply-chain and tariff tensions remain a long-term wildcard.

holdings.name: Strategy Inc
holdings.short_term_strategy: Do NOT add and do NOT panic-sell at the very bottom. MSTR sits at $85.86, just above its 52-week low of $81.81 and down 8.79% on the week. Technically, $81–$82 is critical support; holding above $66.30 while making a clear and confirmed close above $94.20 should take us on a bounce target for MSTR, $116.10. Hold and watch Bitcoin and the Aug 4 earnings; only consider trimming into any sharp bounce above $94.
holdings.long_term_strategy: Over 6–24 months MSTR is a leveraged bet on Bitcoin, not an operating business — its value tracks the ~847,000 BTC on its balance sheet. The 2026 crash (roughly -56% from highs) was driven by Bitcoin's slide and growing fears that the company must keep issuing new shares (dilution); Strategy began 2026 with a $2.25 billion liquidity pool; that figure has declined to $900 million. The clearer 2026 U.S. crypto regulatory framework is a structural positive, but only accumulate if you have high risk tolerance.
holdings.rationale: This week's risk-on rally lifted indexes but NOT MSTR, because its decline is crypto- and balance-sheet-specific rather than macro. With the Fed on hold (steady rates remove a tailwind for speculative crypto) and dilution fears front-and-center, the prudent move is to hold an already-small 7-share stake through the Aug 4 report rather than realize a deep loss at the lows.
holdings.cost_basis_note: Deeply underwater: avg cost basis $323.04 vs $85.86 now, an unrealized loss of about -73%. Because the position is only 7 shares and a small dollar amount, selling here locks in a near-total loss; hold and treat as a high-risk lottery ticket on Bitcoin.

Analyst targets cluster around $300–$350. The regulation loosens restrictions on the export of Nvidia H200 chips to China, a tailwind, though export policy remains a political wildcard. Continue accumulating.
holdings.rationale: This week's rotation OUT of mega-cap AI created the dip — a gift for long-term buyers, not a thesis-breaker. With the Fed steady (stable rates support growth-stock valuations) and AI capex still booming, buying weakness in the sector leader is the right move; the only caution is the Aug 26 earnings and ongoing U.S.-China chip-export politics.

holdings.name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF

Even with PCE inflation elevated and the Fed on hold, broad U.S. equities have absorbed the shock — so the boring, consistent DCA plan continues to be the highest-probability path to wealth.
holdings.cost_basis_note: Profitable: avg cost basis $498.90 vs $685.38, about +37% unrealized gain. Healthy gains confirm the DCA strategy is working; keep adding regularly rather than waiting for a dip that may not come.

benchmarking.subtitle: What Winning Investment Clubs Do Differently

clubs_researched.name: BetterInvesting / NAIC National Network
clubs_researched.strategy: Stock Selection Guide (SSG) methodology — a standardized study of ~5 years of sales and EPS (Earnings Per Share — a company's profit divided by its shares) growth required before any buy vote, removing emotion from decisions.
clubs_researched.tool: BetterInvesting Stock Selection Guide tool + online community and 90-day free trial
clubs_researched.takeaway: A formal written study before every purchase has, per BetterInvesting, empowered hundreds of thousands of individual investors and stops impulse buying.

clubs_researched.name: Black Investment Club @ Harvard Business School (BIC)
clubs_researched.strategy: Builds pipelines into venture capital, private equity, and public markets; partners with the African American Student Union (AASU) on a flagship annual conference connecting alumni, students, and practitioners.

covered_calls.title: Covered Call Strategy
covered_calls.subtitle: Weekly Options Income on Club Holdings
covered_calls.market_iv_context: IV (Implied Volatility — the market's expectation of how much a stock will move; higher IV = richer option premiums) is mixed in late June 2026. After major geopolitical shocks (the Iran conflict) and an AI-stock rotation, single-name volatility is elevated on names like MSTR and NVDA even as broad-index volatility eases on the U.S.-Iran de-escalation. IMPORTANT CLUB NOTE: a covered call requires owning at least 100 shares per contract. FI Community currently owns 7 MSTR, 10 NFLX, 6 NVDA, and ~24.6 VOO — below 100 shares each — so the plays below are EDUCATIONAL setups to learn the mechanics now and execute once a position reaches 100 shares.
covered_calls.covered_call_primer: A covered call means selling someone the right to buy 100 of your shares at a set 'strike price' by a set expiration date, in exchange for cash today called the 'premium.' Key terms: STRIKE PRICE = the price your shares could be sold at; PREMIUM = the cash you collect upfront and keep no matter what; DTE = Days To Expiration; OTM = Out of The Money (a strike above today's price, so there's room to rise); annualized yield = the premium scaled to a full-year rate for comparison. If the stock stays below the strike, you keep your shares AND the premium. If it rises above the strike, your shares get 'called away' (sold) at the strike — you still profit, just capped.
